sam (eng-runtime): heads-up — saw a regression on qwen2.5 after the kernel-selector change last night. p95 token latency doubled for some long-prefix multilingual batches. profiler points at KV-cache miss rate spike when rope_scaling=dynamic. repro & sample output below.

maria (eng-runtime): numbers? which model config + batch sizes?

sam (eng-runtime): p50 ~ 45ms -> 70ms, p95 ~ 140ms -> 340ms for seq_len~1024, batch=8 (mixed CJK + en). baseline kernel was stable-kv-layout, new autotune picked autokernel-v2.

kevin (eng-ml): any evidence of head/kv_head mismatch? last time we saw this it was a kv stride indexing bug.

sam (eng-runtime): logged runtime header on a repro run: 
```
MODEL=qwen2.5
HEADS=32
KV_HEADS=16
ROPE_SCALE=dynamic
KERNEL=autokernel-v2
BATCH=8
SEQ=1024
```
profiler snippet: 
```
KV_index_misses: 74%
KV_cache_hits: 26%
KV_stride: 2

stack: runtime::kernel_selector -> kv_cache::get_shard(index=63) -> memcpy -> kernel_dispatch
```

linh (eng-runtime): hmm that KV_stride=2 seems suspicious. autokernel-v2 assumes interleaved kv layout for kv_heads==heads, but here kv_heads != heads. selector should have fallen back but looks like it didn't.

maria (eng-runtime): can you reproduce with kernel forced to stable-kv-layout? quick A/B test please.

sam (eng-runtime): running now. forcing KERNEL=stable-kv-layout -> p95 back to 150ms, KV_miss 12%. so autokernel-v2 is the trigger.

kevin (eng-ml): autokernel-v2 probably optimized for ropescale=none or static. dynamic ropescale changes per-position offsets; if kernel assumes contiguous kv packing it will compute wrong offsets -> reads cross-head leading to misses and extra mem ops.

linh (eng-runtime): good hypothesis. can we add a guard in selector: if kv_heads != heads || rope_scaling!=static -> force stable-kv-layout? quick patch reduces blast radius.

sam (eng-runtime): local patch applied, rerun microbench: latency and KV hit numbers match baseline. patch diff: 
```
if (cfg.kv_heads != cfg.heads || cfg.rope_scaling != "static") {
  pick("stable-kv-layout");
}
```

perf-bot: nightly-regression-test: autotune-suite failed on qwen2.5 (flaky kernels) — triggered by commit ab12f4c (kernel-selector heuristics). See CI: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/1234

maria (eng-runtime): plan: revert kernel-selector change in canary for hosted, pin dedicated pools to stable-kv-layout, run full autotune with added invariant checks for kv_layout compatibility. I'll own rollout. @kevin @linh please prepare the tests and a short regression test that asserts kv_stride==1 when kv_layout==interleaved.

kevin (eng-ml): will add a unit that simulates head/kv mismatches + dynamic ropescale and assert selected kernel matches layout.

linh (eng-runtime): I'll draft a hotfix to selector with the guard + telemetry that logs when assumptions don't hold (emit metric: selector_assumption_violation). Add an alert at 5x baseline rate.

sam (eng-runtime): created a quick reproducer gist: https://gist.redwood/xyz (contains run script + perf logs). tagging this as P1 for the runtime perf board.

maria (eng-runtime): timeline: revert to stable in canary within 1h, monitor p95 and selector_assumption_violation, if green push to prod after 3h of stable.

linh (eng-runtime): also adding a small integration test to nightly that runs mixed-ling batch with seq=1024, kv_heads=16, heads=32, rope_scaling=dynamic.

sam (eng-runtime): thanks. logging the issue: https://issues.redwood/INF-789. add notes about kernel-selector heuristics and expected layout invariants.

perf-bot: incident created INF-789, severity=sev3 (performance regression).

maria (eng-runtime): TL;DR — autokernel-v2 incorrectly chosen for qwen2.5 variants with non-equal kv_heads and dynamic RoPE. Hotfix: guard selector -> stable-kv-layout + telemetry. Follow-up: tighten autotune invariants and add targeted regression tests. :thumbsup:

kevin (eng-ml): also flag for model-team: consider documenting recommended kv_head configs for qwen2.5 variants to avoid accidental mismatches.

linh (eng-runtime): assigning PR to me, will link in INF-789. anyone else seeing this on other models (mixtral/mistral)? post here if you do.

sam (eng-runtime): not yet, running cross-model sweep now and will update thread.

maria (eng-runtime): thanks team.
